usages.explain: Uses the speculative form of 「よい」to express the meaning: it might be okay, probably no problem. As in example 2, the form 「...がよかろう」 is also used as permission. Young people rarely use this in spoken language.

examples.content: どうせもう遅いんだから、ここには泊まればよかろう。
examples.transcription: どうせもうおそいんだから、ここにはとまればよかろう。
examples.mean: It's already late anyway, so I guess I'll just stay here for the night.

examples.content: 重い家具を持つのは男たちに任せたらよかろう。
examples.transcription: おもいかぐをもつのはおとこたちにまかせたらよかろう。
examples.mean: It would be better to leave the lifting of heavy furniture to the men.

usages.synopsis: Use the speculative form of 「よい」.

title: よかろう => it's okay to have, it's fine even ...
